# Ed's Agentic Finance Rails

> How AI agents connect to money How brokers, banks and payment networks let AI agents trade, pay and manage money, and who approves what. Every fact links to a source card; unconfirmed values say "unknown".

[Curated by Edward Yavno](https://agenticfinancerails.com/about)

How to use it: cite the page and the source card for every fact, say "unknown" when the wiki does, and check page_status and last_verified. Warn if a page is stale or archived, or last_verified is older than 30 days. Not investment advice. Reader's guide: AGENTS.md.

## Feedback

POST a short note to /feedback; instructions at /agents#giving-feedback or GET /feedback.

- [FAQ](faq.md): short cited answers to common questions

## Providers

- [Alpaca](providers/alpaca.md): Alpaca's hosted Trading MCP uses OAuth for live and paper accounts; a local MCP and a CLI use API keys. No broker-side per-order approval is documented.
- [Coinbase](providers/coinbase.md): Coinbase for Agents: a remote MCP with OAuth for allowlisted clients, or a local CLI with an API key. Coinbase enforces trade limits, and a dedicated portfolio is optional.
- [Interactive Brokers](providers/interactive-brokers.md): Remote MCP connector. By default the AI drafts trade instructions you review and submit; eligible accounts can enable Autonomous Trading in an AI Partition.
- [Kraken](providers/kraken.md): Kraken ships a local MCP server with its CLI. It runs on your own machine, can trade live only when you turn on trading services, and asks you to approve each order, withdrawal or transfer.
- [Public](providers/public.md): Public runs a hosted MCP server at mcp.public.com/mcp for Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Meta Muse, Perplexity and Grok. Most apps sign in with OAuth; Muse uses a Public API key. Every trade is a real order, with no paper mode.
- [Robinhood](providers/robinhood.md): Remote Trading MCP with OAuth. Agents read all Robinhood accounts but trade only in a dedicated agentic (MCP) account; per-order approval is an optional toggle.
- [Scalable Capital](providers/scalable-capital.md): Scalable Capital runs an MCP server with four access levels you set in its web app. Buy and sell orders need Full access, and each order needs your fresh, explicit confirmation of a preview.
- [Webull](providers/webull.md): Webull's hosted Cloud MCP prepares trades you confirm in the Webull app; its local OpenAPI MCP places orders directly, with risk limits and a sandbox default.

## Payments

- [Payments](payments/README.md): How AI agents pay: card-network agent programs, payment tokens, wallets, protocols and agent cards, each with a sourced page, plus merchants that ban agents.
- [AgentBank](payments/agentbank.md): An MCP server that lets an AI agent collect, hold, convert and send money, including to bank accounts in local currency, using crypto rails. The owner confirms every payment, and an approval threshold adds an extra check.
- [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments](payments/agentcore-payments.md): AWS service that lets an agent pay for APIs, MCP servers and content over x402 and MPP within a per-session budget. Since 2026-11-19 it can also pay AWS Marketplace sellers in US dollars on the AWS bill, with no crypto wallet.
- [Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP)](payments/agentic-commerce-protocol.md): An open standard for buyers, their AI agents and businesses to complete purchases. OpenAI and Stripe maintain the spec, which is in beta.
- [AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol)](payments/ap2.md): An open protocol that records what a user authorized an agent to buy as signed mandates: a Checkout Mandate for the merchant, a Payment Mandate for payment.
- [ChatGPT Wallet](payments/chatgpt-wallet.md): OpenAI's wallet that lets an agent in ChatGPT pay for you. You approve each purchase with a biometric check, and the card network supplies a payment token so the agent and merchant never see your real card number.
- [Lightspark Agent Accounts](payments/lightspark-agent-accounts.md): Lightspark accounts where an AI agent holds, spends, sends and receives money within limits and approvals the account holder sets. It pays Visa merchants with a card valid for one purchase. Sold to companies that build agents.
- [Link wallet for agents](payments/link-wallet-for-agents.md): Stripe's Link wallet for agents lets a person approve each purchase an agent makes, with a one-time card or shared payment token. Muse, Grok Bot, Instinct and Claude Duet use Link or a wallet like it.
- [Mastercard Agent Pay](payments/mastercard-agent-pay.md): Mastercard's program for agent payments. Agents are registered and verified before they can pay, and they pay with agentic tokens. Merchants can verify agents with Web Bot Auth.
- [Merchants and outside agents](payments/merchants-and-outside-agents.md): Some merchants forbid AI agents from buying. eBay, United and Booking.com ban them without permission, and Target allows only a short list of approved agents.
- [PayPal](payments/paypal.md): PayPal offers an MCP server, run locally or hosted, and an agent toolkit that let AI agents use PayPal business APIs such as orders, invoices, subscriptions and disputes.
- [Rain Agent Vaults](payments/rain-agent-vaults.md): Rain's funded balance for AI agents. The owner funds a vault and sets rules, and the agent pays with a single-use virtual Visa or Mastercard card issued for each purchase. Sold to companies that build agents.
- [Robinhood Agentic Credit Card](payments/robinhood-agentic-credit-card.md): A virtual card inside the Robinhood Gold Card that your AI agent uses through the Robinhood Banking MCP. You approve each purchase or set a required monthly limit.
- [Stripe](payments/stripe.md): Stripe offers shared payment tokens, which give a seller scoped, time-limited use of a customer's payment method for agent purchases, plus an official MCP server at mcp.stripe.com.
- [Visa Intelligent Commerce](payments/visa-intelligent-commerce.md): Visa's agent payments program: approved agent builders get tokenized Visa credentials, network-level controls and consumer-approved purchase instructions.
- [x402](payments/x402.md): An open payment standard built on HTTP 402 Payment Required: the server asks for payment inside the request, and the client pays and retries. Coinbase uses it.

## Personal money agents

- [Personal money agents](personal-money/README.md): AI agents that work with a person's bank and card data, the tools that connect them, banks' own AI tools, and how big banks treat outside agents.
- [Banks and outside agents](personal-money/banks-and-outside-agents.md): What news reports say about big US banks blocking or limiting outside AI agents, including Chase's block on agents shopping with a card number, the read-only middle ground, and the US data-rights rule in the background.
- [Finances in ChatGPT](personal-money/chatgpt-finances.md): Finances in ChatGPT reads your accounts through Plaid and credit reports through Experian, in the US. OpenAI says it cannot move money, pay bills, trade or change account settings.
- [Claude Duet](personal-money/claude-duet.md): Claude Duet is Anthropic's proactive agent app, in research preview. It asks before it pays, sends or deletes, pays with a one-time Link card, and cannot trade or move money between accounts.
- [Claude Personal Finance](personal-money/claude-personal-finance.md): Claude's Personal Finance feature reads your balances and transactions from banks you link through Plaid, read-only. It cannot move, manage or invest money. It is in beta on paid US plans.
- [Gemini with Google Wallet](personal-money/gemini-google-wallet.md): Google's Gemini app can read your spending from Google Wallet and linked bank and card accounts to answer money questions. It is read-only and cannot move money.
- [Grok Bot](personal-money/grok-bot.md): Grok Bot can read balances, spending and investments from accounts you link through Plaid, read-only. It can also pay with a Link one-time card or X Money, with a prompt to approve each purchase.
- [Instinct](personal-money/instinct.md): Instinct is a personal assistant that works in iMessage and WhatsApp. Plaid says it powers read-only account connections for US users, and Stripe says Link helps power its payments.
- [JPMorgan Smart Cash](personal-money/jpmorgan-smart-cash.md): A JPMorgan Chase AI tool in a targeted pilot. Per a news report, it aims to predict a user's cash flow and move funds to maximize yield. Only a news source is cited.
- [Meta Muse](personal-money/meta-muse.md): Meta's personal AI agent. Its finance features use Plaid so people can connect bank, card, investment and mortgage accounts for personalized money guidance.
- [Nous](personal-money/nous.md): A UK household AI agent that tracks bills and subscriptions, switches providers and cancels services for you. You choose how much it decides on its own. It reads bank data through an FCA-regulated open banking provider but cannot move money.
- [OpenAI dots](personal-money/openai-dots.md): OpenAI's dots are always-on agents with their own cloud computer. They can buy with a card saved on a merchant site after approval. Whether a dot can read your Finances data is unknown.
- [Perplexity Personal CFO](personal-money/perplexity-personal-cfo.md): Perplexity lets people connect accounts through Plaid and ask about their own money, read-only. Plaid reports it in the US with Perplexity Computer and in 17 European countries as Personal CFO.
- [Plaid MCP servers](personal-money/plaid.md): Plaid's MCP servers are developer tools: a hosted Dashboard MCP for diagnostics and a local sandbox MCP. They do not give agents access to users' accounts.
- [Starling Assistant](personal-money/starling-assistant.md): Starling Bank's in-app AI assistant will set up payments from voice or text, and the customer approves each one with a tap. It reaches all retail customers by the end of 2026.
- [X Money](personal-money/x-money.md): X Money is a US money account inside the X app, run by X Payments LLC with Cross River Bank. Through the Grok Bot plugin, an agent can read the balance and history, and send or pay with approval per action.

## Approval models

- [Approval models](approval-models/README.md): The five ways brokers decide who approves an agent's order, from a walled-off account to no broker-side approval at all.
- [Approval model: AI Partition](approval-models/ai-partition.md): An eligible client funds a partition inside their account where a connected AI may submit supported orders without approving each one.
- [Approval model: draft, then you submit](approval-models/draft-then-submit.md): The agent writes a non-binding trade instruction; nothing happens until you review and submit it yourself in the broker's app.
- [Approval model: none at the broker](approval-models/none.md): The broker executes what the agent sends. Any approval step has to live in your agent, MCP client or local server.
- [Approval model: per-order confirm](approval-models/per-order-confirm.md): The agent prepares each order, and a person confirms it in the broker's own app before it reaches the market.
- [Approval model: separate account](approval-models/separate-account.md): The agent can only trade in an account or portfolio you create and fund for it, so its reach is capped by what you deposit.

## Rails

- [Rails](rails/README.md): The building blocks under agent access to money - how agents connect, authenticate, pay, prove who they are, and carry a user's mandate.
- [Agent identity](rails/agent-identity.md): How agents can prove who they are to websites and merchants - signed HTTP requests, network-run trust protocols and proof-of-human delegation.
- [Agent payments](rails/agent-payments.md): Starter overview of how agents pay - card-network agent programs, scoped payment tokens, open commerce protocols and HTTP 402 payments.
- [Institutional markets](rails/institutional-markets.md): How AI agents negotiate and trade between firms, starting with a pilot Treasury bill negotiation by BNY and Microsoft in which humans approved the final terms and the agents could not execute.
- [Local MCP servers and CLIs](rails/local-mcp-and-cli.md): Self-run MCP servers and CLIs authenticate with API keys you hold, so their guardrails are only as strong as your local setup.
- [Mandates and data access](rails/mandates-and-data-access.md): Protocols that record what a user authorized an agent to do, and the US data-rights rule that may shape agent access to bank data.
- [Remote MCP with OAuth](rails/remote-mcp-oauth.md): How hosted broker MCP servers advertise their OAuth setup, how AI clients register with them, and why a broker's allowlist of clients still matters.

## Build it

- [Build it](build/README.md): Practical notes for engineers and coding agents connecting to broker MCP servers safely.
- [Connect an MCP client](build/connect-an-mcp-client.md): The connection commands and server URLs each launch broker documents for MCP clients, from the providers' own setup pages. Start with paper or sandbox.
- [Human-in-the-loop patterns](build/human-in-the-loop.md): Where to put human approval in an agent trading flow, and why broker-side approval beats client-side approval.
- [Starter prompts](build/starter-prompts.md): Copy-paste prompts for AI assistants: questions this wiki can answer, then prompts for coding agents. Cite pages and say unknown rather than guess.

## Comparisons

- [Comparisons](comparisons/README.md): Side-by-side views of how providers handle approval, read access and safety for AI agents. Every value is sourced or says unknown.
- [Launch brokers compared: approval and safety posture](comparisons/launch-brokers.md): Side-by-side view of how the five launch brokers let agents trade, who approves orders, and where the guardrails are enforced.

## Analyses

- [Analyses](analyses/README.md): Saved answers to questions asked of the wiki, each with cited sources, starting with a comparison of the AP2, ACP and x402 agent payment protocols.
- [AP2 vs ACP vs x402: which AI agent payment protocol does what?](analyses/ap2-vs-acp-vs-x402.md): AP2, ACP and x402 compared side by side. What each agent payment protocol does, who maintains it, what it costs and its limits, with a sourced table and FAQ.

## What changed

- [What changed](changelog/README.md): Every update to the wiki, newest first, with the current size of the wiki in numbers. Generated from page headers.
- [What changed: 2026-11-22](changelog/2026-11-22.md): Stripe's chief economist shared Link agent-wallet spend figures, including nearly 80-fold growth from September to mid-November.
- [What changed: 2026-11-21](changelog/2026-11-21.md): The starter prompts page now has research questions and coding-agent prompts, the front page has a Try a starter prompt link, and Coinbase has a table of which AI apps trade the most.
- [What changed: 2026-11-20](changelog/2026-11-20.md): Citi and Chase user agreements, Singapore's planned Know Your Agent protocol, AWS AgentCore payments, Lightspark, BNY and Microsoft's Treasury bill negotiation, and six more updates.
- [What changed: 2026-11-19](changelog/2026-11-19.md): Chase's reported block on agents that shop with a card number, how Stripe's Link gets around it, adding a Chase card to ChatGPT Wallet, connecting eight providers from your AI app, new pages for Public, Scalable Capital and Kraken, and Mastercard's developer MCP server and Agent Pay for Machines.
- [What changed: 2026-11-18](changelog/2026-11-18.md): Coinbase Agent Controls and ChatGPT confirmation cards, Public's order gate, Visa Agentic Ready, a live Mastercard flight purchase, Plaid Agent Detection, Gemini, Starling and Wealth.com, plus Grok Bot, X Money, Claude, ChatGPT Finances, dots, Instinct and Perplexity.
- [What changed: 2026-11-17](changelog/2026-11-17.md): A comparison of the AP2, ACP and x402 agent payment protocols, question-style headings, answer-first openings, shorter page descriptions and an Updated date label.
- [What changed: 2026-11-15](changelog/2026-11-15.md): A shorter front page, a trading-only Trading page, a cited FAQ, record tables, a What changed home page, search and agent metadata, and new pages on ChatGPT Wallet, Rain Agent Vaults, AgentBank, Nous and merchants that forbid agents.
- [What changed: 2026-11-14](changelog/2026-11-14.md): Added Payments and Personal money agents sections with one page per program, a What we cover overview on the front page, official ERC-8004, a glossary, and a front-page refresh.
- [What changed: 2026-11-13](changelog/2026-11-13.md): Added a thin advisor-agents section, a third-party Schwab RIABiz source, official Coinbase agent-feedback docs, and related official and third-party source cards.
- [What changed: 2026-11-12](changelog/2026-11-12.md): First draft of the wiki - five launch broker pages, 103 source cards, approval-model taxonomy and agent packaging.
